clips.provenance: NYT Visual Investigations 'How Israeli Soldiers Killed 15 Rescue Workers in Gaza' (2 May 2025). Centrepiece is the phone video filmed by PRCS paramedic Rifaat Radwan from inside a moving ambulance, Tel al-Sultan, Rafah, before dawn 23 Mar 2025; recovered from his phone after his body was found in a mass grave. NYT: multiple soldiers fired over six minutes at unarmed emergency workers who posed no threat. IDF initially said vehicles approached 'without headlights or emergency signals'; its 20 Apr 2025 probe cited 'professional failures' and dismissed a deputy commander (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-military-says-review-into-killing-gaza-aid-workers-found-professional-2025-04-20/). Forensic Architecture/Earshot (Feb 2026): at least 910 rounds over two hours, no return fire (https://forensic-architecture.org/investigation/the-massacre-of-aid-workers-in-tel-al-sultan).

segments.desc: night dashcam-style phone view from an ambulance: headlights on a sandy road, a red fire engine and ambulances ahead with emergency lights flashing
segments.notes: lights-on proof that refutes the IDF's first account; burned NYT subtitles (Rifaat's words) at the bottom: crop the lower 15% or keep them deliberately. clips.provenance: ITV News report (23 Jan 2024), Khan Younis, al-Bahr Street outside al-Aqsa University, in the IDF-designated 'safe zone'. A group of men walking with hands up and a white flag is fired on; Ramzi Abu Sahloul is shot dead. Filmed by ITV cameraman Mohammed Abu Safia (ITV) and videographer Ahmed Hijazi (NBC, CNN). Earshot audio-ballistic analysis: 6 shots, two or more shooters in Israeli Army vehicles ~330 m east of the camera (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pie8S-VPh7U). NBC geolocated it and filmed tanks lining the road; IDF told NBC it was 'not aware of this incident' and 'the video is clearly edited' (https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/gaza-palestinian-israel-white-flag-shot-dead-killed-rcna135419). CNN: 'impact of the first round ... appears to come from the direction of the tanks' (https://www.cnn.com/2024/01/26/middleeast/hala-khreis-white-flag-shooting-gaza-cmd-intl).

Attribution is CNN's eyewitness+satellite case, not ballistic. Note: the brief's 'ITV' attribution for this clip is wrong; ITV covered Ramzi Abu Sahloul.
